consistency_findings: Main per-protocol secondary-outcome counts reproduce the article summary: 28 statistically significant lower-risk associations, 4 statistically significant higher-risk associations, and 27 non-significant associations after Benjamini-Yekutieli correction.

The sensitivity analysis was directionally consistent overall; glaucoma and erectile dysfunction changed from non-significant in the main analysis to statistically significant in the sensitivity analysis, as stated in the main text.

Intention-to-treat estimates were generally more attenuated than per-protocol estimates for the primary outcomes; eTable 7 does not provide an intention-to-treat estimate for total number of hospitalisations.
extraction_limitations: The atom model represents one normalized quantitative estimate per atom. Adjusted comparative estimates were normalized; crude estimates are preserved in quantitative_result.original_result_text rather than emitted as separate atoms.
eTable 8 summarizes prior literature. Those secondary reports were not converted into primary-study atoms because the current source did not generate those underlying results.
Supplementary file 3 is a reporting checklist and was reviewed for coverage but not atomized as study evidence.
No external sources were used to fill missing study details.
schema_gaps: No dedicated field exists for corrected/multiplicity-adjusted p-values, so the Benjamini-Yekutieli context is preserved in effect_measure/tags and p_value or p_value_text.
No dedicated fields exist for person-time or incidence rate; these are preserved using ArmObservation.value/unit and original_result_text.
No dedicated study-level target-trial-emulation object exists; design details are represented as method atoms.
